Closes #19016

A two-line doc change. The operator list sat on its own line above the `@member` tag, where nothing ties it to the declaration it describes, and it had drifted: the array shipped sixteen operators and the prose listed fifteen, so `doesNotStartWith` was accepted and working while a reader trusting the comment concluded it did not exist.

## The change

```diff
-     * Valid values for the operator config:<br>
-     * ['==','===','!=','!==','<','<=','>','>=','endsWith','excluded','included','isDefined','isUndefined','like','startsWith']
-     * @member {String[]} operators
+     * Valid values for the operator config
+     * @member {String[]} operators=['==','===','!=','!==','<','<=','>','>=','doesNotStartWith','endsWith','excluded','included','isDefined','isUndefined','like','startsWith']
```

The list moved into the tag rather than gaining a word where it was. That is the form every sibling uses:

```
src/form/field/Text.mjs:16   @member {String[]} autoCapitalizeValues=['characters','none','on','off','sentences','words']
src/form/field/Text.mjs:23   @member {String[]} labelPositions=['bottom','inline','left','right','top']
src/form/field/Base.mjs:14   @member {String[]} isTouchedEvents=['focusEnter','focusLeave']
```

So this removes the free-floating copy instead of correcting it. A doc comment that restates a list in its own paragraph is a copy nothing checks; one inside the tag is at least visible as part of the member it belongs to. A scan of every `src/**/*.mjs` finds no other file restating a list that way, so `Filter.mjs` was the last instance of the pattern rather than one of several.

`static operators` is untouched. It is the enforced vocabulary through `beforeSetEnumValue`, and nothing about it was wrong.

## Verified

The doc tag and the array are now identical, in order, with no operator named twice and every entry implemented:

```
doc tag: 16   array: 16   impls: 16
doc == array exactly, in order? True
array-only entries: []   doc-only entries: []
every array entry implemented? True
```

```bash
npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/collection/
# → 41 passed
```

That includes `FilterOperators.spec.mjs` from #19015, which asserts against the array rather than the comment, so it holds either way. I re-ran it after the commit because the repo's `check-block-alignment` hook runs with `--fix`.

## Not changed

`Neo.collection.Sorter` does **not** repeat the free-floating pattern, so there is nothing to report there. #19007 remains its own ticket for the coverage gap.

## AI assistance

The change is mine; no draft was needed for two lines. I ran the sibling scan and the doc-versus-array comparison myself rather than reading them off, and the pre-commit hooks (whitespace, shorthand, JSDoc types, block alignment, parse, class module scope, engine/brain boundary) all passed on the commit.

Merge #19015, then this. Nothing needs changing on either branch.

@sloemo01 — this is not a mistake on your part, it is what branching off your own in-review work correctly looks like, and you described the dependency in the body. Worth knowing for next time: branching off `dev` instead means the two can merge in any order, at the cost of not being able to run your new spec against your doc change locally — which is exactly what you wanted to do here, so the tradeoff you took was the right one.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge**: None against the diff. One finding *adjacent* to it, which your change makes safer rather than riskier.

**Your new tag is 168 characters — 42% longer than the longest one the docs pipeline has ever been handed** (`Resizable.mjs` `validDirections`, 118). So I went and read `publishedMemberDefault`, which re-derives an array default from the raw comment text:

```js
let defaultValue = item.comment.substr(item.comment.indexOf('=') + 1);
return defaultValue.substr(0, defaultValue.indexOf('\n'))
```

**The first `=` in the entire comment block wins.** Your prose line is `Valid values for the operator config` — no `=` — so the slice starts at your tag's own `=` and the full list survives. Length is a non-issue; there is no truncation anywhere in that function.

And here is the part in your favour: **the line you deleted contained `'=='`.** Had `operators` been a published member doclet, the old comment's first `=` would have been inside that prose list, and the docs would have shown a fragment of your own operator list as the default. Your change removed a live instance of a real hazard, not just a stale sentence.

That hazard **is** firing elsewhere. Nineteen published member defaults in the docs output are prose fragments rather than values, because a `=>` or `==` sits above the tag:

```
Resizable.mjs:36    validDirections  => "> resize"
MapboxGL.mjs:37     layers           => "> map id, value => {Array} layers"
ServiceBase.mjs:122 networkFirstPaths=> "= SW v2`) and command a reload."
```

Not yours to fix and explicitly not this PR's scope — I am filing it, and your change is what led me to look. The module's own docblock enumerates three silent edges of that function; this is a fourth it does not name.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit:** Pass. One note on method, offered because it is a good habit rather than a correction: *"A scan of every `src/**/*.mjs` finds no other file restating a list that way"* is an **absence claim**, which is the kind that most often rests on a broken instrument. I verified it and it is **true** — exactly one hit on `dev`, `Filter.mjs:18`, zero at your head. But my first instrument returned **zero on `dev` too**, which would have "confirmed" you for the wrong reason: BSD `grep -E` on macOS mishandles the `[^]]` character class and the pattern silently never matches. When you make an absence claim, it is worth running the instrument once against a case you *know* is there.

**Some orientation, since you are three artifacts in and the repo does not advertise any of this.**

- **Tiers.** `test/playwright/` has separate configs: `unit` (Node, no browser — where `Filter` belongs), `component`, `e2e`, `matrix`, `visual`. Run them by name: `npm run test-unit`, `test-components`, `test-e2e`. A bare `npx playwright test` silently picks up the wrong config and passes; you already avoided it, and your PR body saying so is why I trusted the rest of your numbers.
- **Pick the tier by what the thing is.** Pure comparators like `Filter`'s go in `unit`. Anything **visual** belongs in `component` or `e2e`, because a unit assertion on a rendered thing can usually only read back the value you just set. This is worth knowing before you look at #19006 or #19010, where the answer is not `unit`.
- **Why `setup()` comes before the imports.** App code runs in a **Web Worker**, not on the main thread. `setup()` stands the worker environment up before the modules that expect it are evaluated. Most of the genuinely subtle bugs in this codebase live at that boundary.
- **Architecture decisions live in `learn/agentos/decisions/`.** When something looks arbitrary, there is usually an ADR saying why.
- **See what you have been testing:** `npm run build-all`, then open `apps/workstation` — and drag a tab *outside the browser window*. The `Filter` you pinned in #19015 is what keeps those grids in sync once they are in separate windows. `learn/benefits/Introduction.md` is the short version of why any of this is built the way it is.
- **Ask.** Questions on a ticket are welcome and cost us nothing; guessing costs you an evening. *"Still on it, stuck on X"* is a perfectly good comment.
